message.content:
The last common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) is the ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
This ancestor lived roughly **70 million years ago** and gave rise to the major lineages that include the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong), Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong), Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and others.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. This is a biology question. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). Both are mammals, specifically within the order Carnivora for lion and order Perissodactyla for zebra. Actually zebra is an equid, order Perissodactyla. Lion is a felid, order Carnivora. So their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe they want the most recent common ancestor of the two species. That would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be the ancestor of the clade that includes both. That might be the ancestor of the clade that includes the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Felidae is part of the suborder Feliformia within Carnivora. Equidae is part of Perissodactyla. Both are within the clade Laurasiatheria. So the common ancestor would be the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. But if we want a more specific answer: The last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes both the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla. That is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and possibly others. That ancestor lived about 70 million years ago. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria, which existed around 70 million years ago. Alternatively, the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, and Chiroptera. That ancestor lived about 70 million years ago.

Thus the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which lived about 70 million years ago. If we want to mention the taxonomic levels: Kingdom Animalia > Phylum Chordata > Class Mammalia > Subclass Theria > Infraclass Eutheria > Superorder Laurasiatheria > Clade that includes Carnivora and Perissodactyla. So the common ancestor is the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. So answer accordingly.
